1.why: All eight screens show a clean static layout with solid header, white card, and no moving images, animations, or pop-ups.

2.why: Primary actions use high-contrast dark-blue buttons and clear headings that stand out against the light background.

3.why: Each step presents a single focused form or confirmation so the needed field or button is immediately visible.

4.why: The user must remember and manually carry a long recovery token from the log/link to the verify field and later an MFA code, requiring multi-step recall.

5.why: No password-manager hints, autofill attributes, or “remember me” options appear on any password or code entry screen.

6.why: Aside from the email field retaining its value on step 2, there are no recognizable saved-password or familiar-account cues.

7.why: Labels and instructions are short, use plain language, and are easy to read on every screen.

8.why: No error messages or validation feedback are shown in any of the provided screenshots.

9.why: Password rules are stated as text but no input examples, format masks, or sample tokens are supplied.

10.why: The flow offers only password-plus-MFA; no alternative choices such as code, face, or other login methods are presented.

11.why: Each screen contains at most one input field and one primary button, avoiding simultaneous choices.

12.why: Green success text, confirmation pages, and growing log entries clearly state the outcome of each action.

13.why: Brief instructional sentences appear on most steps, yet there are no contextual help tips, tooltips, or progressive guidance for new actions.

14.why: Forms remain editable so a user can re-enter data, but no explicit “try again” or undo controls are provided.

15.why: Every screen re-uses the identical header, card layout, button style, and footer, keeping the design consistent throughout.
